desc: Sort intervals by right endpoint while retaining each interval's original index; build the parallel array of right endpoints for binary search.
Precompute predecessor p(i) for each sorted interval as the count of intervals with right endpoint strictly less than l_i (strict r < l, so touching endpoints are rejected).
Define DP with exact counts k=0..4; each cell stores (best_weight, lexicographically-smallest sorted index tuple); impossible states marked with weight -1.
Implement transitions per sorted interval i: skip (carry DP[i-1][k]) and take (DP[p(i)][k-1] + weight_i, inserting original index in sorted order); compare by weight then lexicographic tuple.
At the end compute global max weight over exact k=0..4 and pick the lexicographically smallest tuple (Python tuple ordering gives shorter-prefix-is-smaller), returning it as a list.
Verify provided examples return exactly [2,3] (weight 8) and [1,3,5,6] (weight 21).
Cross-check the DP against exhaustive subset enumeration (sizes 0..4) on 20000 random small inputs with touching endpoints present: zero mismatches.
Timing check at n = 5*10^4: runs well under a second with modest memory.
